notes: kind is permanent or day (24 hours). code is optional: without it the server picks one. Typed codes are cleaned up like at unlock (spaces, dashes, small letters). folder is the folder it sends into, and must be given (400 bad_request without). With shows_folder, guests with the PIN also see and download what is in the folder (but delete nothing); it is false unless given. Errors: pin_format (400), pin_taken (409): codes are never used twice; not_found (404) for no such folder. For a PIN that shows an encrypted folder, secret is what the PIN link's secret brings (the link is /#<code>.<secret>, the secret 32 random bytes in base64url): {"locked": the secret locked with a key from version version of the folder's private key (share-e2ee-v1/pin-secret, folder:<id>:<version>), so only someone who holds it can make one, "version": …, "root": the root locked with the secret (aad root), "keys": [{"version", "locked": that version of the folder's key locked with the secret}]}; only with shows_folder (400 otherwise), 409 key_outdated for a version the folder doesn't have. A new code (/new-code) keeps the secret. In the answer (and in GET /api/pins), secret is {"locked", "version"} for such a PIN, so an admin's device can open it with the folder's key and show the whole link again; null otherwise. A PIN that only sends into a folder with keys gets the root's fingerprint after the code in its link instead (/#<code>.<the first 16 bytes of SHA-256 of the root, base64url>), which the admin's device adds to link.
